comparison: Perfect agreement on DuSTER methodology (C4, C39, C40, C64-C66). Both evaluations find the method well-supported and effective for analyzing low S/N particles like NPM2. Reviewers explicitly acknowledged DuSTER's utility without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic interpretations of NPM2 structural variants (C58, C77-C79). Both accept these as reasonable inferences from structural data. Reviewers affirmed the mechanistic insights without challenging the interpretations.

Perfect agreement on NPM2 structural limitations (C89-C90). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers acknowledge modest map quality and partial H1.8 density as honest assessments. Reviewers explicitly noted these caveats while accepting the structures as valid.

Strong agreement on NPM2 structural findings (C5-C6, C41-C45, C52-C57, C75-C76). Both find the pentameric structure, open/closed variants, and structural details well-supported. Reviewers accepted the findings despite noting modest map quality, which OpenEval also addresses in R14.

Perfect agreement on NPM2 biological background (C46-C51, C69, C74). Both accept these literature-based contextual claims as appropriately supported by citations. Reviewers did not challenge these background statements.

Strong agreement on prior work context (C17-C21, C23-C24). Both accept these claims about the authors' previous chromatin work as well-supported by citations. Reviewers explicitly acknowledged the Arimura et al. 2021 foundation.

Perfect agreement on chromatin structural comparisons (C31-C32, C34-C37). Both find the interphase/metaphase comparison and structural findings well-supported. Reviewers explicitly affirmed the negative result showing no apparent differences between conditions.

Strong agreement on method limitations (C80-C85). Both accept these as honest assessments. Reviewers explicitly noted the transparent discussion of limitations including formaldehyde fixation, recombinant protein use, and potential bead effects, viewing this positively.

Strong agreement on MagIC-cryo-EM technical implementation (C27-C29, C33, C60-C63). Both find the spacer design, magnetic concentration, and stated advantages well-supported. Reviewers praised the method as 'innovative,' 'clever,' and 'convincing' with no challenges to technical claims.

Strong agreement on problem statement and method rationale (C1, C8-C12). Both accept these claims establishing the concentration requirements problem. Reviewers affirmed the significance for 'studying native macromolecules present at low concentrations,' implicitly accepting the problem statement.

Strong agreement on biological interpretation of NPM2-H1.8 findings (C38, C43, C68, C70-C71). Both find the integration of MS, biochemical, and structural data supporting interphase-specific enrichment and mechanistic insights. Reviewers affirmed these findings without challenge.

Divergent evaluation on speculative Cdk1 phosphorylation claim (C72). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of experimental validation, while peer reviewers accept it as appropriate speculation in discussion context alongside C73. Peer review groups C72 with C73 as reasonable hypotheses.

Strong agreement on scientific context claims (C7, C13-C16). Both accept these background claims about chromatin biology and ChIP limitations as appropriately supported by citations. Reviewers did not challenge these contextual statements.

Strong agreement on workflow limitations (C86-C88). Both accept these as honest technical assessments. Peer review groups these with other limitations (C80-C85) and views the transparent discussion positively.

Strong agreement on quantitative sample requirement claims (C59, C67). Both find the 100-1000 fold improvement well-supported by experimental data and appropriate citations. Reviewers affirmed the concentration reduction as a key methodological advance.

Partial overlap on chromatin application data (C22, C30, C32). OpenEval groups these with broader chromatin findings (C3, C31-C37), while peer review groups them with overall method validation (C2, C27-C29, C33, C59-C63, C67). Both find claims well-supported.

Partial overlap on NPM2 background (C25-C26). OpenEval groups these with broader NPM2 literature context (C46-C51, C69, C74), while peer review groups them with authors' prior chromatin work (C17-C21, C23-C24). Both find claims well-supported.

Minimal overlap on interphase-specific NPM2 enrichment (C38, C43). OpenEval groups these with comprehensive NPM2 structural findings (C5-C6, C41-C45, C52-C57, C75-C76), while peer review groups them with biological interpretation (C68, C70-C71). Both find claims well-supported.

Minimal overlap on speculative model (C73). OpenEval finds C73 supported as appropriately cited speculation, while peer review groups it with C72 as reasonable discussion hypotheses. Both accept the speculative nature as appropriate.
